question: Which of the following correctly describes the relation between frequency (v)and time period ( T )?
solution:
The correct answer is __**v T = 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Frequency (v)** is defined as the **number of complete oscillations** or cycles of a wave that occur in a **unit of time** (usually **one second**).
 
• **Time Period (T)** is defined as the **time taken** by a wave to complete **one full cycle** or oscillation.
 
• The relationship between **frequency** and **time period** is **reciprocal**. This means that as the time period of a wave increases, its frequency decreases, and vice versa.
 
• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as **v = 1/T**. When we rearrange this equation by multiplying both sides by **T**, we get the product **v T = 1**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• If the relationship was **v T = 0**, it would imply that either the frequency or the time duration is **zero**, which is not possible for a physical wave. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The expression **v / T = 1** suggests that frequency and time period are **directly proportional** and equal, which contradicts the laws of physics. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The expression **v + T = 1** is incorrect because **frequency (1/s)** and **time (s)** have different physical dimensions and cannot be added together in a standard physical equation. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Units**: The **SI unit** of **frequency** is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named after the **German physicist Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**. **1 Hz** is equal to **1 cycle per second**. The unit of the **Time Period** is the **second (s)**.
 
• **Wave Speed Formula**: The speed of a wave is determined by its **frequency** and **wavelength (λ)**, represented by the formula **Speed = v × λ**.
 
• **Angular Frequency**: In many physics applications, **angular frequency (ω)** is used, which is related to frequency by the formula **ω = 2πv** or **ω = 2π/T**. It is measured in **radians per second**.
 
• **Audible Range**: For a human ear, the standard **audible frequency range** is between **20 Hz** and **20,000 Hz**. A frequency of **20 Hz** corresponds to a **Time Period** of **0.05 seconds**.
 
• **Dimensional Analysis**: In **dimensional formulas**, **Time (T)** has the dimension **[T]**, and **Frequency (v)** has the dimension **[T⁻¹]**. Their product results in a **dimensionless constant** of **1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inverse Relationship**: A high-frequency wave (like **Ultraviolet rays**) has a very **short time period**, whereas a low-frequency wave (like **Radio waves**) has a **long time period**.
 
• **Periodic Motion**: This relationship is fundamental to all types of **periodic motion**, including the movement of a **simple pendulum**, the vibration of a **guitar string**, and **electromagnetic radiation**.
 
• **Practical Application**: In **electronics**, the clock speed of a **processor** is measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**. A **1 GHz** processor completes **1,000,000,000 cycles** in **one second**, meaning the **Time Period** for a single cycle is **1 nanosecond (10⁻⁹ s)**.
